title: Add perf-canary regression coverage for quantization profiles (baseline vs enabled)
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
## Context
Quantization Profile Library is opt-in at the route level, with safe fallback to baseline precision when incompatible/disabled. Before beta expands beyond design partners, we need automated performance coverage to catch regressions introduced by:
- new profile versions (INT8/FP8 mix)
- runtime kernel selection changes
- control plane/profile resolution behavior changes (metadata fetch, caching)

This ticket adds perf-canary scenarios that run baseline vs profile-enabled execution for a fixed set of models/hardware and fails loudly on meaningful regressions (tail latency, throughput, VRAM, error/fallback rate).

## Goal
Add deterministic perf-canary coverage that compares:
1) Baseline (feature off / default precision)
2) Quantization enabled with a pinned profile_ref (no aliases)

…and emits clear failure signals + alerts with enough context to quickly triage (which model/profile/GPU/SKU/workload, which metric moved, and by how much).

## Scope
- Add canary scenarios/jobs covering: prefill+decode latency, throughput, VRAM headroom, error rate.
- Run across representative GPU SKUs (at minimum: L4 and H100 in benchmark lab; A10 if available in canary env).
- Pin exact model version + quant_profile_id (no "recommended" / "latest") to keep comparisons stable.
- Record and export key metrics to existing dashboards referenced in ENG-5817.
- Configure alert thresholds and routing (SRE + runtime/perf owners).

Out of scope:
- Quality scoring (belongs to eval harness + guardrails policy); perf-canary will only validate perf + correctness signals.
- Automatic rollback actions (we only page + annotate release gate; rollback remains manual per runbook).

## Proposed scenario matrix (v1)
Scenarios are meant to be small, repeatable, and sensitive to regressions:
- Model A (chat): 8k context (mixed prompt), 256 tokens decode
- Model B (gen): 2k context, 512 tokens decode (decode-heavy)
- Model C (embedding/rerank): short context microbatch to validate batching interactions

Each scenario runs twice per SKU:
- baseline mode
- quant enabled (profile pinned)

## Metrics to compare
Perf-canary will compute deltas between baseline and quant enabled within the same run window.

Primary gates (hard fail):
- p95 end-to-end latency: quant enabled must be <= baseline * 1.07 (<= +7%)
- p95 decode latency (tokens/s inverted): must be <= baseline * 1.08 (<= +8%)
- throughput (req/s at steady load): must be >= baseline * 0.92 (>= -8%)
- runtime error rate (5xx + runtime exceptions): <= 0.2% absolute and <= baseline + 0.1%

Secondary gates (warn + annotate, do not fail by default):
- VRAM peak usage: quant enabled should not exceed baseline + 10% (warn if exceeded)
- fallback_rate (resolved but not applied): should be < 0.5% (warn at 0.5–2%, fail at >2%)
- profile metadata fetch rate-limit events: should be 0 (warn on any)

Correctness signal (hard fail):
- "applied" must be present in runtime logs/traces for > 98% of requests in quant scenario (to avoid silently measuring baseline)

Notes:
- Thresholds intentionally allow small overhead from profile loading/extra guards but catch the regressions we saw in earlier spikes (decode tail inflation + cache interaction).
- We should keep thresholds SKU-specific if we see consistent differences (start global, then tune).

## Alerting
- Failures should:
  - block the release gate for runtime-1.18 canary promotion
  - page #eng-sre-oncall during business hours if failing 2 consecutive runs
  - post to #eng-runtime with the summary table

Alert payload must include:
- model_id + model version
- quant_profile_id
- GPU SKU + driver/cuda label
- scenario name
- baseline vs quant metrics + deltas
- links to traces/logs (request ids) and dashboard panel

## Implementation notes
- Ensure we read quant_profile_id from runtime annotations (see PR adding quant_profile_id log fields) rather than inferring from config.
- Avoid registry thundering herd: canary must use warmed metadata cache where possible; include a "cold start" run only if we want to exercise that path intentionally.
- Use the same prompt seeds across runs for determinism.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] New perf-canary scenarios exist for baseline vs quant enabled on at least two GPU SKUs.
- [x] Canaries pin explicit profile ids and model versions.
- [x] Failure thresholds implemented for p95 end-to-end and decode latency, throughput, error rate.
- [x] Fallback/application correctness signal validated via runtime log annotation.
- [x] Alerts routed to SRE + runtime channel with actionable context.
- [x] Runbook link included in alert description (rollback procedure + kill-switch steps).

## Links

- Rollback runbook: sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/rollback-procedure-quantization-profiles.json
- Runtime selection design: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/quantization-profile-selection-in-runtime.json
- Perf suite standard: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/quantization-profile-perf-benchmark-suite.json

comments: 2025-02-14 (Leila Farouk): Drafted scenario matrix. Need final list of pinned profile ids from Applied ML that are expected to be stable for 4+ weeks (avoid "recommended" alias).
2025-02-18 (Jonas Weber): +1 to adding decode-heavy scenario; prior regression showed up only after ~300 decoded tokens. Suggested we split metrics into prefill p95 and decode p95 if possible.

2025-02-21 (Aisha Bello): Alert routing proposal: warn in #eng-runtime on first failure; page SRE if 2 consecutive failures or if error rate gate trips. Please include fallback_rate and metadata fetch failures in alert payload even if not gating at first.

2025-02-26 (Hiro Tanaka): Kernel path differences between baseline and INT8/FP8 mix are expected; thresholds should be SKU-dependent if L4 shows slightly higher overhead. Start with +8% decode p95 and revisit after a week of data.

2025-03-03 (Leila Farouk): Implemented correctness signal check using quant_profile_id + resolution outcome (applied/fallback/disabled). Found 4% fallback due to sequence length cap in one scenario; adjusted workload to stay within profile max_context for gating scenarios. Keeping the out-of-bounds workload as a non-gating informational run.
2025-03-07 (Connor O'Brien): Confirmed release gate wiring: failing canary blocks promotion to 10% on runtime-1.18 train. Added link to rollback runbook in the gate description.

2025-03-12 (Leila Farouk): Landed changes in perf-canary PR and validated in staging: baseline vs quant comparisons are stable across 3 runs; no flakes observed. Next: let it run for 48h to establish baseline bands before turning on paging.
2025-03-19 (Aisha Bello): Enabled paging condition (2 consecutive failures) + added dashboard deep links. Marking ticket done.
